title: Conditional mutual information is invariant under a.e. equal variables
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X,X'$, $Y,Y'$, and $Z,Z'$ be measurable random variables on $\Omega$ taking values in countable (discrete) measurable spaces, each attaining only finitely many values. If $X = X'$, $Y = Y'$, and $Z = Z'$ hold $\mu$-almost everywhere, then the conditional mutual informations agree: \[ I[X : Y \mid Z;\, \mu] = I[X' : Y' \mid Z';\, \mu]. \]
hypotheses_covered: value spaces are countable and discrete
X, Y, Z, X', Y', Z' are measurable
replaced:
Under a probability measure, if $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} X'$, $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Y'$,
and $Z =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Z'$, then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = I[X' : Y' \mid Z';\mu]$.
